glossary.canonical curriculum: The versioned source package used to create learner delivery and standalone projections.
glossary.legacy curriculum: Earlier module/lesson content retained as read-only evidence while canonical delivery is active.
glossary.work context: The active role through which a user is operating.
glossary.institution context: The active institution against which staff authority is revalidated.
glossary.learning context: The personal or institution scope to which new progress is attributed.
glossary.membership: A user-to-institution relationship; it grants no staff power without a current role assignment.
glossary.institution role: Learner, Instructor, or Institution Admin authority attached to an active membership.
glossary.content author: A separately assignable shared-curriculum capability, not an institution role.
glossary.system admin: The single global platform role with cross-institution administrative authority.
glossary.attempt: One versioned activity submission or self-check event in a specific learning scope.
glossary.progress: A bounded state such as viewed, attempted, self-checked, or completed; it is not synonymous with mastery.
glossary.deliverable package: The one active package that passes the environment-specific curriculum release guard.
glossary.draft preview: A visibly labeled non-production curriculum view; never evidence of production approval.
glossary.targeted invitation: An expiring, revocable, single-use institution invitation bound to one canonical email.
glossary.classroom code: A bounded reusable secret that creates a pending join request rather than immediate membership.
